best_parts: node start_ok: 'I have it, skip the pattern lesson' fast lane straight to occ_probe, so a confident novice is not made to sit through the pattern explanation
nodes start_help, occ_help, zieman_help, lap_help, tr40_help: every hint carries a 'Show me the answer' rung, so no learner is left with only 'Try again'
node tr40_probe: three distractors, each a distinct TR40 error (above and medial, neither, the inguinal position copied across), with feedback that names the anchor-to-tubercle rule
flaws: node lap_probe (TR1): only one trap is offered and TR1 is never re-tested in S3; a tired learner who swaps lateral and medial is not caught again in this segment

nodes occ_probe (TR21), tr40_probe (TR40), start (TR23), wall_probe (TR28): each trap appears on one probe only in this segment, so recovery is never credited on a second form (contrary to the two-probe rule)

node start (option 'Both, since both can reach the scrotum'): it is the weakest of the three choices for someone who knows the scrotum marks the indirect sac, so it is nearly dominated and adds little diagnosis
node explain_pair: three messages and two branch choices in one node, so it carries more than one idea for a learner at 1 a.m.

best_parts: nodes route then vignette_lap: TR1 is tested as a recognition probe and again as a vignette, the two-form retest the rubric asks for
nodes occlusion then occl_vignette: TR21 returns in a mechanism form and then a description form, with the sure_note on each trap
node wall2: the conjoint tendon is found by the posterior-wall role, with internal oblique and external oblique as anterior-wall traps, a clean contrast of the two walls
flaws: hint nodes h_scrotum, h_occl, h_zieman, h_route, h_lap, h_fem offer only 'Try again': a learner who misses twice has no further rung, which is poor for a tired student
no fast lane anywhere in the segment: every learner, however confident, walks all 13 probes
femoral distractors recur in five probes (scrotum, occlusion vignette, route, vignette_lap, femoral_pos), so the TR40 repetition becomes tedious rather than diagnostic
node scrotum (option 'Femoral hernia'): femoral does not descend into the scrotum, so a learner who knows that rules it out at once; the distractor is near-dominated
node t23 and other trap feedback nodes: the path returns to the same probe on 'Try again' with no new hint, so a repeat miss reads as a loop

best_parts: node predict: predict-then-show at the bedside (the finger on the deep ring, then 'does it come back?') is the most clinically real moment in the three variants and asks before it tells
node femoral_t40a / femoral_t40b and hints femoral_hint, wall_hint: each trap is followed by a 'Show me the answer' rung, so the learner is not stuck
node direct_probe: a second bedside test on a new lump, which gives the predict lesson a delayed re-test in a different form
flaws: node scrotal (correct option 'Globular swelling by the tubercle, reduces straight back, rarely scrotal'): it is the longest label and the only one with three features, so the key can be found by length (DP1)
node femoral (correct option 'Femoral hernia'): it is the one short single-term label among long descriptive distractors, so it is findable by form (DP1)
node lap (TR1): a two-option probe with a single trap and no second TR1 probe in S3, so the most important swap in the segment is tested once
node scrotal (TR23) and node wall (TR28): each trap appears once in the segment, so there is no retest in a different form
no fast lane: a confident learner who passes the predict probe is still sent through explain_route and every later probe

merge_ideas: a's start_ok fast lane and full hint ladder, plus b's route/vignette_lap pair for TR1, so the most important trap is retested in two forms and a confident learner can skip
c's predict-then-show bedside opening as the entry to a's path, since it is the most clinically framed entry and keeps the 'Show me the answer' rung
b's occlusion/occl_vignette pair for TR21 added to a, with the femoral distractors trimmed to two probes so TR40 does not repeat five times
b's wall2 posterior-wall contrast as the retest for TR28, replacing a's single wall_probe
